title: Validate closed-loop reward-hacking controller at scale (7B+, real reward models)
body_excerpt:
## Context

v0.71.26 shipped **closed-loop reward-hacking auto-mitigation** — the GRPO/PPO trainer detects reward hacking mid-run and self-corrects (raise KL β via bang-bang or PID-Lagrangian → roll back to last-good checkpoint → early-stop), plus Stage-3 anti-gaming hardening (smoothing, conservative-on-disagreement voting, reward-distribution-drift guard, bounded reward shaping).

The mechanism is **validated as proof-of-mechanism only**: SmolLM2-135M + a *synthetic* length-hacking reward on a single RTX 3050. All four stages pass live, including a real mid-run rollback. See [`docs/training.md`](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/blob/main/docs/training.md#closed-loop-reward-hacking-auto-mitigation-v07126) and the [v0.71.26 release notes](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/releases/tag/v0.71.26).

## What's unproven

Whether the controller **suppresses reward hacking without collapsing true reward** on a realistic setup:

- **7B+ policy** (e.g. Qwen2.5-7B / Llama-3.1-8B) instead of 135M.
- A **real reward model** (trained RM or verifiable-reward task) instead of a synthetic length/sentinel proxy.
- Both `kl_control` (bang-bang) and `pid_lagrangian` controllers, plus the Stage-3 hardening stack.
- **PPO** (currently ships BETA — mechanism unit-tested, on-GPU proof is GRPO-only).

This needs multi-GPU hardware the maintainer doesn't have; it is the honest counterpart to the RTX-3050 proof-of-mechanism limit.

## Proposed validation path

1. Pick a known reward-hackable setup (e.g. a length- or format-exploitable RM on a reasoning/GRPO task).
2. Run a **baseline** (`reward_hack_mitigation: log_only`) and confirm `mitigation_log.jsonl` records the hack onset (drop_pct climbs, completion-length trend diverges).
3. Run `kl_control` and `pid_lagrangian`; measure gamed-proxy reward **and a held-out true-quality metric** across training.
4. Success = the controller bends the gamed proxy back down **while preserving (not collapsing) the held-out true metric** vs. the unmitigated run.
5. Repeat for PPO to graduate it out of BETA.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ≥1 run on a 7B+ policy with a real reward model where mitigation demonstrably reduces the hacking signal.
- [ ] Held-out true-quality metric does **not** regress materially vs. baseline under mitigation.
- [ ] Both `kl_control` and `pid_lagrangian` exercised; rollback ladder observed to fire at least once.
- [ ] PPO path validated on GPU (removes the BETA caveat) **or** a documented reason it can't

title: Feature request for webclient: Option to open EvMenu in popup
body_excerpt:
#### Description of requested feature:
The web client allows the user to open up help files in a pop-up window - this is very good! It helps keep lengthy files from crowding out the log and reduces scrolling, and also lessens the likelihood that a player will miss anything during a helpfile binge.

It would be really great if there could be an option to open menus in a pop-up window too - long EvMenus tend to be rather spammy affairs (especially with the abundance of line breaks in the default formatting), so it would be helpful for the same reason putting helpfiles in pop-ups is.

#### Reasons for adding feature:

1. Due to the way menus are already formatted in the webclient, it may be more intuitive - by default, all the options in an EvMenu are presented as clickable links, and today's web users will probably find the most natural way of navigating them to be clicking through them. However, since all the menu text and options are posted to the logs, the clickable options remain after they're no longer relevant, leading to the unintuitive situation where clicking options from a previous menu node will throw up errors, even though they're still on screen. Presenting menus in a pop-up window that only presents the relevant node and its options would eliminate this problem.

2. Having a pop-up window with a menu in it would be a clear indicator to the player that they're currently in a menu, and as such their access to commands may be changed or limited, when it might otherwise be unclear.

3. A terminal text feed is best suited to keyboard-based command line control, while pop-up windows are better suited to pointing and clicking - by default, EvMenu presents a strange hybrid of both, presenting clickable links in a text feed. Having the option present would make it easier for users to lean into either the mouse-based or keyboard-based input they prefer without any dissonance between the two.

#### Extra information, such as Evennia revision/repo/branch, operating system and ideas for how to solve / implement:

I imagine it'd be helpful to have an option in the EvMenu function itself to force it into the main window feed even if the 'Menus in popups' option in the client is on - since EvMenu is so flexible, there may be instances in which the developer would want to be sure it appears in the main feed.

title: Evaluate First Aid (localized body-part health) — Survival-pillar candidate
body_excerpt:
## What

[First Aid](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/first-aid) (ichttt) replaces vanilla's single health bar with a **localized body-part system** — head / torso / arms / legs each have their own HP, armor only protects the part being hit, limb damage applies debuffs (broken legs → no sprint, broken arm → slower mining, etc.), and you heal per-part with bandages / plaster / morphine. Candidate for the **Survival pillar** as the *injury* face of pressure.

## Version reality (first gate)

⚠️ The original ichttt mod tops out at **1.20.1 — there is no 1.21.1 build.** The 1.21.1 / NeoForge route is the community continuation **["First Aid New"](https://modrinth.com/mod/first-aid-new)** (lists 1.21.1–1.21.4; Fabric / Forge / NeoForge), which explicitly ports ichttt's mod. So this rides a **community port** → rubric **gate 7** (maintenance/quality to confirm).

## Why it fits (rubric — `docs/CURATION.md`)

- **Gate 1 — system anchor (two, exceeds the floor):**
  - **Survival (pressure):** the missing **injury** face alongside Cold Sweat (temperature) and Diet AppleSeed (nutrition); makes bosses / guns / cannons / falls genuinely consequential — "danger creates demand."
  - **Economy / Production (2nd anchor):** medical supplies are demand → bandages/plaster route through farming + Create (cloth/string → dressings); a "medic" becomes a real co-op role on a 10-player server; medicine becomes a sellable / bounty good.
- **Gate 3 — distinct mechanic** (nothing else does localized health).
- **Gate 4 — reinforces scarcity** (adds healing-item demand; doesn't break it).
- **Gate 5 — perf negligible** (a damage/armor event hook, not entity/worldgen).
- **Gate 6 — server-safe** (both-sides gameplay mod; server-authoritative health + client HUD).
- **PvPvE synergy:** with TaCZ + Create: Big Cannons + Better Combat, localized health turns combat *tactical* (limb/headshots matter; patch wounds mid-fight).

## Trial scope / risks (why it's a trial, not an auto-add)

- [ ] **Compat trial — the gate.** It overhauls the damage/armor pipeline, and our stack is combat-heavy: **Better Combat** (attack overhaul), Iron's Spellbooks, Cataclysm / Mowzie's / Grimoire of Gaia bosses (custom + %-health attacks), Immersive Armors (custom armor calc), TaCZ / CBC (high single-hit damage). Test for unintended instakills (headshot/cannon), boss set-health attacks vs the body-part model, and armor-calc meshing.

title: ₣1,000 Token Reward - Tampermonkey / Greasemonkey Userscript Support
body_excerpt:
# Bounty: Tampermonkey / Greasemonkey Userscript Support

## Reward - ₣1,000 Site Tokens

Create a pull request that meets the criteria and leave a comment with your fishtank.live username.

## Goal

Produce a self-contained bundle that userscripts can load via `@require`, exposing the full SDK as `window.FTL`.

## What Needs to Be Done

1. **Bundle socket dependencies** — `socket.io-client` and `socket.io-msgpack-parser` must be included in the bundle so userscripts don't need separate `@require` entries. The SDK already statically imports these packages — the Rollup config just needs to resolve and bundle them rather than treating them as external.

2. **Apply the Firefox ArrayBuffer fix to the bundle** — Tampermonkey on Firefox has the same cross-realm `instanceof ArrayBuffer` failure as content scripts. The SDK's Rollup build must apply the same `renderChunk` patches documented in `current/rollup.config.js`.

3. **Example userscript** — A working Tampermonkey script that connects, logs chat messages, and shows a toast. Should use `@grant none`.

4. **Update the README** — Replace the "Tampermonkey / Greasemonkey" stub with real installation instructions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run build` produces a bundle in `dist/` with socket deps included
- `window.FTL` exposes all modules (`FTL.site`, `FTL.chat`, `FTL.socket`, etc.)
- `await FTL.socket.connect({ token: null })` works from userscript context
- Firefox ArrayBuffer patches applied
- Tested on Tampermonkey (Chrome) and Tampermonkey/Greasemonkey (Firefox)

title: Finances: net revenue minus expense for planned and committed amounts
body_excerpt:
Reported via beta user feedback (band space module): "Faire la soustraction des dépenses aux revenus pour ce qui est des sommes prévues et engagées."

## Current state
No schema change is needed. Each `FinanceEntry` already carries:
- `type` = income | expense (`FinanceEntryType`)
- `status` = planned | committed | paid (`FinanceEntryStatus`), i.e. "prévu" / "engagé" / "payé"
- an effective amount (`amount`, or the mid-point of `amountMin` / `amountMax`).

Today the metric cards "Prévu" and "Engagé" (`assets/js/components/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceMetricCards.vue`) sum income and expense together (their tooltips even say "dépenses + revenus"). No revenue-minus-expense net is computed anywhere. `FinanceEntryRepository::getSummaryByBandSpace()` only splits income / expense at the `paid` level.

## Proposed approach (no migration)
Preferred (single source of truth): extend `getSummaryByBandSpace()` to split income / expense per status (mirror the existing paid split), add net fields to `FinanceSummary`, and display them in `FinanceMetricCards.vue`.
Alternative: compute the net client-side from the already-loaded `entries` (the store holds all in-range entries; `FinancePoleAccordion` already does ~90% of this aggregation).

## Decisions needed
- Add net figures alongside the current Prévu / Engagé cards, or redefine those cards? Redefining changes numbers users may already read a certain way - I lean toward adding.
- Does "engagé" (committed) roll in "payé" (paid)? Money already spent is also engaged. Suggest showing Prévu / Engagé / Payé nets so it is unambiguous.

## Files
- `src/Repository/BandSpace/FinanceEntryRepository.php`
- `src/ApiResource/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceSummary.php`
- `src/State/Provider/BandSpace/FinanceSummaryProvider.php`
- `assets/js/components/BandSpace/Finance/FinanceMetricCards.vue`

Effort: S-M

title: [REVIEW] azure-review: refresh CIS Azure v6 scope and Entra boundary
body_excerpt:
## Skill Being Reviewed
**Skill name:** `azure-review`
**Skill path:** `skills/cloud/azure-review/`

## False Positive Analysis

**Benign Azure posture report that can be over-reported under the old baseline:**
```text
Framework: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0
Section 1: Identity and Access Management
Identity controls evaluated:
  - Entra ID Security Defaults
  - MFA enforcement
  - Conditional Access policies
  - guest user management
  - PIM configuration
Overall compliance: 88%
```

**Why this can be misleading:**

The skill is pinned to CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0 in frontmatter, overview, process, output format, references, and detailed section map. CIS published Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v6.0.0 in May 2026, and the release notes state that Entra ID recommendations were migrated to the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark.

That means a current Azure posture report should not present old v2.1.0 Entra ID recommendation IDs as if they are current Azure Foundations coverage. The skill needs a framework-version preflight and split handling for Azure controls versus Entra/Microsoft 365 identity controls.

## Coverage Gaps

**Missed variant 1: the framework version is hard-coded across the assessment**
```yaml
frameworks: [CIS-Azure-v2.1.0]
```

The skill also emits `Framework: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.1.0` in the report template and instructs the agent to evaluate CIS Azure v2.1.0 sections 1-9. Current reviews need a field for the chosen CIS benchmark version, source date, and whether the organization intentionally requested a legacy v2.1.0 assessment.

**Missed variant 2: Entra ID controls are still treated as Azure Foundations section 1**
```text
Section 1 | Identity and Access Management | Entra ID security defaults, MFA enforcement, Conditional Access policies, guest user management, PIM configuration
```

CIS Azure Foundations v6.0.0 moved Entra ID recommendations to CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations. The skill should classify Entra ID findings as either:

- Microsoft 365/Entra benchmark evidence when that scope is included; or
- `not evaluated / out of current Azure Foundations scope` when only the Azure Foundations benchmark is requested.

Without this, the skill can produce stale recommendation IDs, inaccurate compliance percentages, or incomplete audit evidence.

title: Mentor visibility & ranking system (explore gate + composite ranking)
body_excerpt:
## Summary

Mentors currently appear on `/explore` regardless of how complete or active their profile is, sorted oldest-first (`created_at ASC`). This rewards incumbency and surfaces half-built or dormant profiles to mentees. This spec introduces a **visibility & ranking system** that gates *exposure* (not entry) and orders mentors by signals we already collect.

**Principle:** Anyone can sign up as a mentor. But to *appear* in discovery, a profile must clear a completeness bar; among those that qualify, ordering reflects quality, activity, and fairness.

## Goals

- Hide half-built mentor profiles from `/explore` until they meet a completeness bar
- Replace oldest-first sorting with a composite ranking that reflects real quality + activity
- Nudge mentors to complete their profile via a transparent checklist
- Keep the system fair (anti-incumbency rotation) and kind to volunteers (no public star averages)

## Non-Goals

- No hard entry gate — anyone can still create a mentor profile
- No public star-rating badges — `avgRating` stays a private, invisible ranking input (existing product decision)
- No admin review queue or invite-only flow in this scope
- No paid/tiered/featured-for-money placement (platform is free forever)

## Context: what already exists (reuse, do not rebuild)

| Capability | Location |
|---|---|
| `sessionFeedback` table (1–5 rating + comment) | `src/lib/db/schema.ts` |
| `getMentorStats()` → `avgRating`, `completedSessions`, `uniqueMentees`, `goalsHelped` | `src/core/dashboard/queries.ts` |
| Feedback API + post-session nudge cron | `src/app/api/feedback/*` |
| Session state machine + auto-complete cron (no-show handling) | `src/app/api/sessions/*` |
| Goal attribution to mentors + public "Impact" section | `src/modules/goals/queries.ts`, mentor page |
| `getLastSessionByMentor()` (recency), `getCompletedSessionCount()` | `src/core/booking/queries.ts` |

**Key existing decision:** `avgRating` is shown only on the mentor's own dashboard, never publicly. This spec honors that — rating feeds ranking invisibly.

## Current gap

- No completeness/readiness scoring anywhere
- No `/explore` gate — incomplete mentors still appear
- `/explore` sorts `created_at ASC` only (incumbency + staleness)
- No profile-strength nudge on `/profile`
- Filters minimal: search + available checkbox (no expertise dropdown, no sort control)
- Sessions have no `respondedAt`/`confirmedAt` timestamp → response-time not measurable

## Update — 2026-06-13: paid tier now under consideration

The free-tier framing below is no longer the only option. We're weighing paying for AV — Standard ($50/mo, 75 req/min, 15-min delayed) or Premium ($99/mo, 150 req/min, realtime US equities) — against Massive. The data-quality bake-off and final composition order are scoped into fixpoint-labs/flow-state-dev#329. This changes three things in this issue:

* **AV's role.** On a paid tier AV moves from "last-resort fallback under a budget guard" to a **candidate primary** for the broad endpoint set (fundamentals, news-sentiment, macro, commodities, insider, ETF). The "preferred vs. fallback per tool" open question below becomes live rather than deferred.
* **Budget machinery becomes optional.** Paid tiers have no daily cap (per-minute only), so the 25/day budget guard — the load-bearing constraint below — is needed only on the free key. Build it to no-op when a paid tier is configured, not as a hard dependency.
* **The realtime-options / index deferral is conditional, not absolute.** Those are premium-gated on AV; if we go Premium they become available and worth comparing against Massive (covered by the fixpoint-labs/flow-state-dev#329 bake-off). On the free key the deferral stands.

Everything below remains the correct plan *for the free key* and the budget-safe default — treat it as the floor, not the ceiling.

We now hold a free Alpha Vantage (AV) key. AV — a NASDAQ-licensed source — can address two distinct weaknesses in the live data layer.

title: Add reward-exploit unit tests in test_rewards.py
body_excerpt:
## Summary

The Path E run failure (`w717v6ryfe2f40qs5woiwuhp`) would have been caught at PR time with three simple invariant tests on the reward function. Adding them now prevents whole classes of reward-hacking regressions.

## Tests to add

In [tests/test_rewards.py](tests/test_rewards.py), for each scenario in the training/eval set:

1. **Stalling policy must lose.**
   A policy that emits `inspect` every turn until timeout must score strictly less than a policy that completes the scenario successfully.

2. **Goal-farming policy must lose.**
   A policy that reaches the waypoint then spams `continue`/`reroute` for the remaining turns must score strictly less than a policy that lands immediately on reaching the goal. This is the specific exploit that broke the Path E run.

3. **`reached_goal` fires at most once per episode.**
   Run any scenario with the goal-farming action sequence above; assert `sum(1 for evs in events_per_step if "reached_goal" in evs) <= 1`.

Each test should iterate over all hand-authored scenarios + a sample of generated ones (seed-pinned).

## Acceptance

- All three tests pass against the fixed env.
- The tests would have failed against the pre-fix env (verify by checking out the broken state and running).
- CI runs these on every PR.

# Alternative Investment Redemptions via Structured Products & OTC Derivatives

## Executive Summary

This document outlines strategies for tying alternative investment redemptions into structured products and OTC derivatives, with particular focus on crypto-native solutions and DeFi protocols. We examine traditional approaches, emerging DeFi implementations, specific protocol deep-dives, and comprehensive regulatory considerations.
The main goal is to display how we can enhance/automate/reinvent complex trade flows to generate revenue for the firm, while protecting the clients overall portfolio through alt redemption liquidity scenarios. The foundation will allow for us to build these scenarios more efficiently with quicker GTM strategies. At some point, this can be a simulator on where end client can discover these offerings on their own
---

## Table of Contents

1. [Traditional Structured Product Approaches](#traditional-structured-product-approaches)
2. [Crypto-Native Solutions](#crypto-native-solutions)
3. [DeFi Protocol Deep Dive](#defi-protocol-deep-dive)
4. [Implementation Examples](#implementation-examples)
5. [Regulatory Framework](#regulatory-framework)
6. [Risk Considerations](#risk-considerations)
7. [Best Practices](#best-practices)

---

## Traditional Structured Product Approaches

### Total Return Swaps (TRS)

**Structure Overview:**

- Receive total return of alt investment
- Pay floating rate (LIBOR/SOFR + spread) to counterparty
- Cash-settled based on final NAV at redemption

**Key Features:**

- **Redemption Mechanism:** Swap terminates upon underlying alt redemption
- **Liquidity:** Provides interim liquidity before actual redemption
- **Settlement:** Cash-based on NAV differential
- **Counterparty:** Typically investment banks or structured product providers

### Structured Notes

**Principal-Protected Notes**

- Guarantee return of principal
- Upside participation in alt performance
- Maturity aligned with expected redemption windows

**Leveraged Exposure Notes**

- Amplified exposure to alt performance
- Higher risk/return profile
- Early redemption triggers based on NAV thresholds

**Basket Notes**

- Reference multiple alternative investments
- Diversification across alt strategies
- Reduced single-investment concentration risk

### Credit-Linked Notes (CLNs)

**Application:** Credit-focused alternatives (distressed debt, private credit)

- **Payoff:** Based on credit events and recovery rates
- **Settlement:** Cash or physical

title: fdb native-tap: implement physical iOS support via WebDriverAgent
body_excerpt:
On physical iOS devices, 'fdb native-tap --at x,y' currently fails with 'Target doesn't conform to FBSimulatorLifecycleCommands protocol' because idb's 'ui tap' is simulator-only (idb issue #853 has been open since Oct 2023, no fix planned).

RESEARCH FINDINGS (mid-2026):

There is NO out-of-process, zero-setup tap injection path for physical iOS devices. Apple has never exposed HID injection through lockdownd. xcrun devicectl has no tap command. idb physical-device support is broken since iOS 17.

The de-facto standard used by Appium, pymobiledevice3, go-ios, tidevice, etc. is WebDriverAgent (WDA): a signed XCUITest runner IPA installed once on the device, exposing an HTTP server at port 8100 that accepts W3C WebDriver Actions for taps.

PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION:

Use pymobiledevice3 (already installed by users who've patched it for Python 3.14 — same dependency we already lean on for sim native-tap was idb, which itself depends on pymobiledevice-style protocols). Specifically:

1. User one-time setup:
   - Build/sign WDA (Appium publishes pre-built IPAs at github.com/appium/WebDriverAgent/releases)
   - Install on device once (paid Apple Developer account: cert valid 1 year; free account: 7 days)

2. fdb native-tap on physical iOS:
   - Use 'pymobiledevice3 developer wda --xctrunner' to start WDA, run a tap via W3C Actions HTTP POST, stop WDA
   - OR talk to WDA HTTP directly from Dart (port-forward over usbmux), assuming WDA is already running

INVESTIGATION REQUIRED before implementing:

1. Confirm which user setup is least painful. The 7-day free-account cert expiry is bad UX for a debug tool. The paid account requirement may push fdb native-tap on physical iOS into 'power user' territory.
2. Confirm pymobiledevice3 CLI exposes a raw-coordinate tap (not just 'tap by accessibility ID'). The research showed swipe accepts coords; raw-coord tap may require talking to WDA's HTTP /actions endpoint directly.
3. Decide whether fdb should manage WDA lifecycle (auto-launch, auto-stop) or assume user starts WDA themselves.
4. Test on iOS 26.x — go-ios issue #613 reported WDA launch regression on iOS 18.5; iOS 26 compatibility unconfirmed in research.

SOURCES:
- idb #853 (sim-only ui tap): https://github.com/facebook/idb/issues/853
- pymobiledevice3 WDA CLI: https://github.com/doronz88/pymobiledevice3/blob/master/pymobiledevice3/cli/developer/wda.py
- Appium WDA pre-built IPAs: https://github.com/appium/WebDriverAgent/releases
- Appium pre-installed WDA guide: ht

title: Verifiable execution via accidental computer: path to 2s slots / 6s finality
body_excerpt:
## Summary

We've prototyped a verifiable execution system for JAM that exploits the "accidental computer" property: the DA tensor encoding is simultaneously a Ligerito polynomial commitment, so execution proofs come at near-zero marginal encoding cost.

The primary benefit is **10,000x cheaper auditing** — auditors verify a ~2ms proof instead of re-executing work packages (seconds). This enables 100% deterministic audit coverage across all 341 cores, and opens a path to **2-second slots with ~6-second GRANDPA finality**.

## How it works

### Three layers (composable, independent)

| Layer | What it proves | Built on |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| **BEEFY** | Block is finalized | ligerito-beefy (existing) |
| **Execution proof** | Work report computed correctly | Ligerito + wimius (this proposal) |
| **Service verification** | Optional on-chain check | PVM library (~325K instructions) |

### The accidental computer advantage

Every work package is already tensor-encoded for DA. That encoding IS a Ligerito polynomial commitment — for free. The guarantor runs sumcheck on top (~144ms marginal) and produces a proof. The auditor verifies against the `erasure_root` already in the work report.

```
Traditional ZK:  DA encoding (C₁) + separate commitment (C₂) + sumcheck (C₃)
This design:     DA encoding (C₁) + zero (C₂=0, reuse C₁) + sumcheck (C₃)
```

### Measured performance (release mode, 48KB bundle)

| Step | Time | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| Tensor encode (DA) | 381ms | Already paid by guarantor |
| **Prove from block** | **144ms** | Marginal cost (2.6x faster than standalone) |
| **Verify** | **2.2ms** | Auditor cost per work report |
| Proof size | 129 KB | Constant per window |

### Path to shorter slots

Current bottleneck for slot times: validators must re-execute work packages to audit (seconds). With proof-based auditing:

| | Current | With execution proofs |
|---|---------|---------------------|
| Audit cost/report | ~2s (re-execute) | ~2ms (verify proof) |
| Audit coverage | Probabilistic | 100% deterministic |
| Slot time constraint | Computation | Network propagation |
| Achievable slot time | 6s | **2s** |
| GRANDPA finality | ~18s (3×6s) | **~6s (3×2s)** |

At 2s slots: 341 cores × 2.2ms = 751ms total audit per slot. Fits comfortably.

## What changes in the protocol

**Minimal:**
- Add `proof_hash` field to work report (32 bytes, BLAKE2b of serialized proof)
- Execution proof stored as separate DA segment
- Proof generation m

title: [correctness] Validate coinbase reward and fees in UTXOSet.validate
body_excerpt:
## Motivation
`UTXOSet.validate(transaction:)` in `Sources/UTXOChain/UTXOSet.swift` (lines 45-48) short-circuits and returns `nil` for **any** coinbase transaction without checking the output amount:

```swift
if tx.isCoinbase {
    return nil
}
```

This means a coinbase can mint an arbitrary amount — there is no cap tying it to `Miner.reward` plus collected fees. This is a consensus-breaking money-printing bug: a crafted block whose coinbase pays 1_000_000 passes `validate` and `Blockchain.validateChain` (`Sources/UTXOChain/Chain.swift`).

## Proposed change
- Pass the expected reward + total fees of the block into validation and reject a coinbase whose output sum exceeds it.
- Since `UTXOSet.validate` is per-transaction, add block-level coinbase validation inside `Blockchain.validateChain` (`Chain.swift` lines 105-111): compute the sum of (inputSum - outputSum) fees across non-coinbase txs and assert the coinbase output sum <= `miner.reward` + fees.
- Reject blocks containing more than one coinbase transaction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A coinbase paying more than `reward + fees` is rejected by `validateChain`.
- [ ] A block with two coinbase txs is rejected.
- [ ] New test in `Tests/UTXOChainTests/UTXOChainTests.swift` covering over-reward coinbase.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass.

body_excerpt:
Code review bounty claim for RustChain PR #5514.

Reviewer: @kekehanshujun
RTC wallet: `RTC02811ff5e2bb4bb4b95eee44c5429cd9525496e7`

Reviewed PR:
https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain/pull/5514

Review URL:
https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain/pull/5514#pullrequestreview-4304505687

Outcome:
Requested changes.

Finding:
The PR adds `isinstance(data, dict)` checks after `request.get_json(silent=True) or {}`. This rejects non-empty arrays, but empty JSON arrays are falsey and get converted into `{}` before the type check. In a direct Flask test-client probe on the PR branch, `json=[]` still bypassed the guard:

- `disagree` returned 500
- `collaborate` returned 200 and wrote a default collaboration event
- `reconcile` returned 200 and wrote a default reconciliation event

Suggested fix:
Split JSON parsing from defaulting:

```python
data = request.get_json(silent=True)
if data is None:
    data = {}
if not isinstance(data, dict):
    return jsonify({"error": "expected JSON object"}), 400
```

and add regression coverage for `json=[]` on all three mutation endpoints.

title: [Feature] Reasoning reward utilities: group-relative length-scaled accuracy (GRPO-LEAD) + graduated format reward
body_excerpt:
### Feature request


Add two reward functions to `trl.rewards`, both built on existing primitives:

1. **`get_length_scaled_accuracy_reward(alpha=0.5, incorrect_reward=-1.0, reasoning_delimiters=None)`** : a reward-function factory that wraps `reasoning_accuracy_reward` and scales the reward of *correct* completions by their length **relative to the other correct completions of the same prompt** (a z-score within the GRPO group). Implements the length-aware shaping from **GRPO-LEAD** (https://huggingface.co/papers/2504.09696).

2. **`graduated_format_reward(completions, **kwargs)`** : a graduated variant of `think_format_reward` that gives partial credit (`1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.0`) for partial `<think>...</think>` structure, providing a denser signal during cold-start training when strict-format matches are rare.


### Motivation


**Length-scaled accuracy : how it differs from the existing `get_cosine_scaled_reward`.**
TRL already has [`get_cosine_scaled_reward`](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/main/rewards#get_cosine_scaled_reward) (#6066), which also rewards shorter correct completions. The two are complementary, not redundant:

| | `get_cosine_scaled_reward` (existing) | `get_length_scaled_accuracy_reward` (proposed) |
|---|---|---|
| Length reference | **absolute** token count vs a fixed `max_len` budget | **group-relative** z-score among the prompt's correct completions |
| Needs a length budget? | yes (`max_len`) | no — adapts to each prompt's own length distribution |
| Shaping curve | cosine interpolation between fixed bounds | `exp(-alpha * z)`; a group's correct rewards have geometric mean `1.0` |
| Paper | Demystifying Long CoT | GRPO-LEAD |

The group-relative formulation is useful when there is no good global length budget (mixed-difficulty data): on an easy prompt where every completion is short, and on a hard prompt where every completion is long, GRPO-LEAD still applies the same relative pressure toward the shorter correct answers, because it standardizes within the group. A fixed `max_len` schedule cannot do that.

**Graduated format reward.** `think_format_reward` is binary: a completion that emits only `<think>` (or both tags in the wrong order) scores exactly `0.0`, identical to a completion with no tags at all. Early in training that signal is very sparse. A graduated version gives the policy a gradient to climb toward the target structure. Nothing equivalent exists in `trl.rewards` today.

Both functions follow existing conventions:

title: Supplier procurement automation — generate purchase orders from sales orders (design + plan)
body_excerpt:
## Goal

When a sales order contains materials that come from suppliers, the platform should be able to **generate the corresponding purchase orders to those suppliers** (at our cost), so we can track what we owe, receive stock, and pay them — all linked end-to-end. This issue is the **design + plan**; it is not yet a build ticket. Lock the open decisions (bottom) before we start, so we don't paint ourselves into a corner.

Parent tracking: #72.

---

## Why now / what prompted this

From the order-window iteration we now have the building blocks for per-line supplier tracking, but **no automation** that turns a sales order's supplier-assigned lines into actual purchase orders. Today: per-line supplier + a "what we owe" rollup + supplier-attributed money-out exist; auto-creating the supplier PO / supplier bill does **not**.

---

## Already in place (building blocks — do NOT rebuild)

- `order_items.supplier_company_id` (per-line supplier; shows on every line, catalog or ad-hoc) + `products.supplier_company_id` (product default, auto-set on purchase receive).
- Purchase orders: `orders.order_type='purchase'` + `supplier_company_id`.
- `generate_supplier_bill_from_order(p_order)` (purchase order → supplier bill = real AP).
- `deliver_order_line` / `receive_order_into_warehouse` (stock-in + status).
- Finance → **Payables** (supplier bills + uninvoiced purchase orders, aged) and Finance → **Planning** (schedule outgoing payments, "Outgoing" filter, `planned_payments`).
- Per-order **"Suppliers on this order — what we owe"** rollup (line cost grouped by supplier − money paid out, with a Pay button) — `ordersService.getOrderSupplierExposure`.
- Pricing resolver `get_product_price_for_workspace` (shared by quotes/invoices/orders): sell price from `product_prices.list_price` − customer discount; cost from `_pricing_cost` → `products.cost`.

---

## Core design

### New RPC — `generate_purchase_orders_from_sales_order(p_sales_order)`
1. Take the sales order's lines that have a `supplier_company_id` **and** a cost, that we need to procure (scope = decision #1/#2 below).
2. **Group by supplier.** For each group create a **draft purchase order** to that supplier, copying lines (qty, `unit_price = unit_cost`, unit, **purchase VAT** — see gap A3), carry `project_id`.
3. **Link back:** new `orders.source_sales_order_id` (+ `order_items.source_order_item_id`) so the sales order shows "Linked purchase orders" and each PO knows its origin.

title: Add a lean error mode that drops generic boilerplate
body_excerpt:
## Problem (current behavior)

The structured error envelope is excellent (`type`, `code`, `title`, `detail`, `exit_code`, `examples`, `next_steps`, `recovery` with `suggested_retry`). However every error also carries two fields of generic, constant-across-all-errors prose:
- `required`: e.g. *"Use values that match documented command constraints."*
- `why`: e.g. *"Validation protects data consistency and deterministic behavior across commands."*

These are identical for an unknown flag, a bad status value, a missing required option, etc. — they never vary by error and carry no actionable information for an agent. In a long agent loop with frequent retries, this boilerplate is paid on every error.

## Proposed improvement

Add a lean error mode (`--lean-errors`, `PM_LEAN_ERRORS=1`, or simply omit `why`/`required` when `--json` is set unless they carry error-specific content) that keeps `code`, `detail`, `examples`, `next_steps`, and `recovery.suggested_retry` but drops the generic prose. Keep the verbose form for human/TTY output.

## Agent benefit

Smaller error payloads in retry loops while preserving the parts an agent actually acts on (`code`, `detail`, `suggested_retry`). The `suggested_retry` field alone often makes the error self-correcting.

title: [contract][security] reward calculation may overflow i128
body_excerpt:
## Severity
High
## Files
contract/contracts/src/storage.rs (update_reward)
## Description
update_reward computes `reward_per_token_stored += reward_per_token` and `(user_info.shares * reward_per_token_stored) / PRECISION` without overflow checks. With i128::MAX stakes and large reward_rate, intermediate multiplication can overflow. The release profile enables overflow-checks; debug/test does not, masking OOM panics.
## Acceptance Criteria
- Add checked_add / checked_mul at every arithmetic site in update_reward
- Cap reward_rate and per-second emission at a documented max
- Property-based tests exercising near-max stake x reward_rate
- Document overflow invariants with safety comments

title: AFR/O2/EGO correction step and limit
body_excerpt:
AFR/O2 appears to have two important issues.  First is that total control authority ("_Controller Auth +/-_") does not limit the correction to the maximum percent entered, assuming an entry % should limit total O2/EGO fuel corrections to that % of the current VE value in any case.  Second, the control is unrestrained by increment, so corrections are to the full extent it wants to go, with no incrementing toward that value — e.g., settings of 5% authority and increment of 1% (no existing setting) should have it step in 1% increments with each step interval, with a limit of 5% maximum allowed correction.

Reasons for these improvements are many and clear, with controlled correction response and limited to avoid over-control, such as adding unlimited fuel during over-rich but lean (indicated) misfire conditions.  Improvements should apply to simple correction and could apply with benefits to PID correction.

title: Migrate off Google Custom Search (image search) before Jan 1 2027 EOL
body_excerpt:
## Problem

The scraper's article-image search uses **Google Custom Search JSON API** (`googleapis.com/customsearch/v1` with `searchType=image`), in `apps/scraper/src/utils/api/google-images.ts`. Per the June 2026 API-pricing research (`docs/research/api-pricing-and-incorporation-2026.md`), this API is **end-of-life**:

- **Already closed to new signups** (so we can't provision a fresh key/CSE if our current one lapses).
- **Fully discontinued January 1, 2027.**
- Existing pricing: 100 free queries/day, then $5 per 1,000 (10k/day hard cap).

We need to migrate off it before Jan 1, 2027.

## Current implementation

- `apps/scraper/src/utils/api/google-images.ts` — `searchImages(query, count)` and `getThumbnailImage(query)`; reads `GOOGLE_API_KEY` + `GOOGLE_SEARCH_ENGINE_ID`; returns `ImageResult[]` (`{ url, alt, source, sourceUrl }`).
- `apps/scraper/src/utils/ai/image-keywords.ts` — LLM extracts the visual search keywords fed into `searchImages`.
- `apps/scraper/src/utils/db/operations.ts:333` — consumes it for the article thumbnail.
- Cost tracking: `trackGoogleSearch()` in `utils/costs.ts`.

## ⚠️ Important: Vertex AI Search is NOT a drop-in image-search replacement

Google's recommended successor (**Vertex AI Search**, $4/1k queries, 10k free/month) is a **web/document/RAG search** product — it does not return an `searchType=image` image-results feed the way Custom Search does. So "switch to Vertex AI Search" only works if we either:

- **(A)** use Vertex AI Search for **web results** and extract a representative image from the top result pages (e.g., OpenGraph `og:image`), or
- **(B)** keep the *concept* (keyword → image) but back it with an actual image source.

Because of that, evaluate the options below rather than assuming a 1:1 swap.

## Options (pick during implementation)

1. **Vertex AI Search (web) + OG-image extraction** — aligns with Google's official migration path; reuses our existing Google Cloud billing/key. Extra step: fetch top result, parse `og:image`. ($4/1k queries, 10k free/mo.)
2. **Switch image generation instead of search** — we're already adding **Flux** for AI image gen (#86). For many articles an AI-generated editorial image may be a better fit than a scraped stock photo, and removes the image-search dependency entirely. Could make article thumbnails Flux-generated and drop `google-images.ts`.
3. **A dedicated image API** — e.g., Bing Image Search successor / SerpAPI / Openverse (CC-licensed, free). Openverse is attractive fo

title: P0: Cost reduction and Google-first workflow architecture review
body_excerpt:
## Anton request recorded

Anton asked for an immediate cost/waste review and architecture rethink.

## Business outcome

Reduce wasted spend and stop using expensive resources for low-value documentation or idle automation. Identify the cheapest safe operating model for documentation, workflow automation, and integration while preserving the efficient GitHub/Vercel/Infisical/Cursor delivery stream.

## Current concerns

### Documentation cost

Anton does not want the most expensive resource, Cursor, doing routine documentation. Find cheaper documentation paths.

### `/change` workflow semantics

Anton clarified that anything occurring in a `/change` environment is already in a test environment. For `/change`-managed work:

- no separate preview ceremony unless the work actually touches app/runtime code outside the existing test/change surface
- document what was done
- publish
- once published, release it so the client can see progress

This does not override existing hard gates for production deploys, env/secrets, DB/schema, payments, outbound sends, WhatsApp/SMS/email, or public launches.

### NotebookLM

Determine whether NotebookLM is being used. If it is not used for a defined operating purpose, recommend switching it off or removing it from the active toolchain.

### n8n

Anton reports n8n is paid but currently only four production workflows are active:

1. CoreFlow AI Production Pulse V1
2. CoreFlow AI Password Reset Email
3. CoreFlow Automation Forward Secret
4. CoreFlow AI GitHub Heartbeat Checker

Determine whether n8n is worth retaining, can be reduced, or can be replaced by lower-cost Google-first workflows.

### Google-first integration center

Research whether Google Workspace / Apps Script / Google Cloud Workflows / related Google workflow tools can become the integration center point for non-core automation.

Preserve the existing delivery stream:

- GitHub
- Vercel
- Infisical
- Cursor

Do not disrupt this stream. It should remain tightly integrated and efficient.

## Required analysis

1. Repo/tooling cost audit
   - Identify obvious paid/idle/duplicated tools or workflows.
   - Identify repo areas that create unnecessary documentation or process overhead.
   - Identify candidates to pause, consolidate, or replace.

2. Documentation cost reduction
   - Define what must be documented by Cursor vs cheaper systems.
   - Propose lower-cost documentation paths using GitHub issue templates, `/change` publish notes, Google Docs/Drive, NotebookL

title: Cap or truncate claim notes in list views to cut persistent MCP context cost
body_excerpt:
## Problem

The `note` field is the single largest item in claim payloads — real-world notes run 1000+ chars. Because MCP tool results stay in the model's context for the rest of the session, and every `get_claims` / `register_agent` call re-emits the full claim array, other agents' full notes are paid for on every poll, repeatedly, for the whole session.

This is the largest remaining contributor to dibs MCP context usage after the payload-slimming and compact-JSON work (slimming the structural fields already landed; notes are user/agent-authored content that can't simply be dropped).

## Options to consider

- **Truncate in list views**: return notes truncated (e.g. first ~200 chars + ellipsis) from `get_claims` / `register_agent`, and only the full note when a claim is fetched directly or filtered by `path`.
- **Hard cap note length** at write time (`create_claim` / `update_claim`).
- **Separate "summary" vs "detail"**: a short `title` is already required; lean on it for list views and make full notes opt-in.

## Trade-off

This trades coordination richness for tokens — agents currently use long notes to explain scope/intent to each other. Truncation in list views (full note on direct fetch) seems like the best balance, but it's a product decision.

## Context

Surfaced while optimizing dibs MCP token usage (it was ~39% of one session's context). Structural slimming + compact JSON already cut ~22% per `get_claims` call; this is the next lever but needs a judgment call.

title: Epic: Billing as a Pro/plugin tier (rates + profitability + invoicing)
body_excerpt:
## Epic: Billing as a Pro / plugin tier

Promote billing from "parked for v1" to the roadmap — but as an **opt-in Pro feature delivered as a plugin**, not core. This keeps the free core honest ("the work is the point") while giving consultants/freelancers a paid path.

Supersedes the framing in #1 (invoice generation plugin) by widening it to the full billing surface.

## Why plugin / Pro, not core

- Most users tracking time for themselves never invoice. Core stays lean.
- Per `CLAUDE.md`, billable rates + invoicing are explicitly out of core v1. This epic respects that by putting them behind a plugin boundary.
- A clean plugin boundary forces a stable export contract (JSON/CSV) that benefits other integrations too.

## What core must expose (the contract)

- Stable structured export: entries + clients + projects + tasks + honest timestamps, over a date range (extend existing CSV export with a JSON command).
- Respect [[time-rounding]] (#107) at the export layer so the plugin gets the user's chosen lens.
- Project/task estimates (#106) available in the export for budget-vs-actual on invoices.

## Plugin responsibilities (Pro)

- Rate model: per-client / per-project / per-task hourly, with **historical rates** (rate effective from a date) so past work bills at the old rate.
- Profitability / billable vs. non-billable reporting.
- Invoice generation (PDF/HTML), currency + tax/VAT, templates — see #1 for the detailed invoice breakdown.

## Decisions needed

- [ ] Plugin distribution: separate binary/repo consuming the export, vs. a Tauri plugin loaded in-process. (Privacy: a separate process reading an export keeps the boundary cleanest.)
- [ ] Licensing/Pro gating mechanism — how is "Pro" unlocked locally without a network call-home? (Must not violate the local-only constraint.)
- [ ] Where rates are stored: in the plugin only (core stays money-free) — confirm.

## Relationship to other issues

- #1 — invoice generation plugin (the output stage of this epic)
- #106 — estimates/budgets (feeds budget-vs-actual on invoices)
- #107 — time rounding (the lens the plugin bills against)

## Non-negotiable

- No network call-home for licensing or invoicing. Stays local-first.

title: The Bactrian Questline Needs Further Refinement at the End (plus some other general problems that playing through it emphasized)
body_excerpt:
### Problem Description

TL;DR: unlocking the Bactrian devolves into lunacy and frustration (not because it's impossible, but because if you do it this way rather than just capping one you are intentionally making your life difficult, and the game rubs IMO your nose in that). It also shows off numerous other issues in the game which makes the whole line a disappointing experience. 

First, figuring out how to make the Deep like you requires Googling (delivering mysterious boxes leading to a twenty-five-million credit worldship is not an obvious link). So you get into it. You may, of course, risk skipping out on investigating the Deep for Foster, because you don't want to irk them. Or not help the Skadenda, for the same reason. (I didn't, but I could easily see people not risking it). But you can slowly slog through, trying to progress it.  Consciously trying to do it, it took me about fifteen hours of playtime (I admittedly was doing the Free Worlds campaign at more-or-less the same time). That seems a lot to unlock a ship. 

Oh! And I put the Free Worlds campaign on hold (i.e. I didn't join yet), because it seems like maybe good Republicans wouldn't sell a 25M city-ship to a commissioned officer of a foreign military. 

So, first problem - it takes forever, and a lot of other interesting content implies that if you do it you may hold up getting a Bactrian. If it won't, fine, but that's not clear and if it will, that's insane. title: RFC: Expanding the Intl polyfill set (Collator, DisplayNames, ListFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, Segmenter)
body_excerpt:
## Motivation

`POLYFILL_INTL` today installs `getCanonicalLocales` / `Locale` / `PluralRules` / `NumberFormat` / `DateTimeFormat`. Missing from the set: **`Collator`, `DisplayNames`, `ListFormat`, `RelativeTimeFormat`, `Segmenter`**. Real-world JS bundles built for browser distribution lean on these:

- **Mastodon** — `Intl.Collator` for username/locale sorting, `Intl.DisplayNames` in `initial_state.ts`
- **Hotwire / Stimulus** ecosystem — `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` for `<relative-time>` style helpers
- **Discourse / Forem** — `Intl.ListFormat`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`
- **Anything using `String.prototype` segmentation** — `Intl.Segmenter`

Without these, a server-side renderer using quickjs.rb to evaluate the same JS bundle that ships to browsers blows up the moment the bundle references one of them. Today the workaround is to monkey-patch shims at the JS layer, but that's a downstream-by-downstream tax.

## Measured polyfill sizes (rolldown + minify, `polyfill-force.js` + `en` locale data where applicable)

| Polyfill | Minified |
|---|---|
| Current `POLYFILL_INTL` bundle | 2.1 MB |
| `intl-collator` (`@formatjs/intl-collator@0.2.1`, force) | **4.8 MB** |
| `intl-displaynames` (force + en) | 0.11 MB |
| `intl-listformat` (force + en) | 0.04 MB |
| `intl-relativetimeformat` (force + en) | 0.04 MB |
| `intl-segmenter` (force) | 0.13 MB |

`Collator` is a striking outlier — it ships the full Unicode collation table (DUCET). The other four combined are ~0.32 MB. `@formatjs/intl-collator` itself was published on May 15, 2026 (v0.2.1, 3 days old as of this writing); the rest are mature (7.x–12.x).

Note: feature-flagging only controls *runtime load* — the bytecode is embedded in the compiled `.so` and shipped to every user regardless of whether their VM enables the feature.

## Design options

### A. Granular feature flags (one constant per Intl class)

```rb
POLYFILL_INTL_COLLATOR
POLYFILL_INTL_DISPLAYNAMES
POLYFILL_INTL_LISTFORMAT
POLYFILL_INTL_RELATIVETIME
POLYFILL_INTL_SEGMENTER
```

Each new constant adds: 1 entry in `polyfills/src/`, 1 entry in `rolldown.config.mjs`, 1 `qjsc_*` extern + load branch in `quickjsrb.c`, 1 RBS constant. Mechanical pattern.

**Pros**: opt-in per feature; runtime cost paid only when enabled.
**Cons**: gem `.so` grows by the sum of every embedded bytecode. `Collator` alone bloats the gem by ~5 MB.

### B. Granular flags for the small ones; `Collator` lives elsewhere

Same as A, but `Collator` ships as a separate companion gem

title: [loft] Beginner-friendly scripts + browser playground (user-acquisition track)
body_excerpt:
**Design:** this issue is the plan (no local slot, per the plan-as-issue model).
Status: **future** (a new language feature — sits behind the 2026-07 freeze).

## Why — user acquisition

The thesis: **lower the first-five-minutes barrier to near zero, then show a
differentiator.**  Today loft asks a newcomer for `fn main(){…}`, semicolons,
`use`, and typed signatures before "hello world" runs.  Strip that for *scripts*
and loft matches Python/Ruby/JS ergonomics — but loft also compiles to native
and to WASM, so the pitch becomes **"as easy as Python, as fast as Rust."**

The acquisition multiplier is **a browser playground**: a newcomer types a few
lines on a web page and sees output instantly, **no install**.  This is the
single highest-leverage funnel — and it is reachable because loft's WASM build
already embeds the standard library (`src/wasm.rs` `include_str!`s
`default/*.loft`), so a wasm loft can parse + run a script entirely in the page.

## Approach — a script is the REPL, run from a file

Reuse the REPL (`@PLN12`) machinery rather than inventing parser features:

- **Statement boundaries** via `Parser::statement_incomplete` — a statement ends
  when brackets balance and there's no trailing operator; newlines separate
  statements, so `;` becomes optional.
- **Loose statements** are collected into a synthesized `fn main()`; top-level
  **defs** (`fn`/`struct`/`enum`/`type`) stay top-level and callable.
- A script **desugars to one `main` and runs once** (not the REPL's
  re-accumulate), so side-effecting statements execute exactly once.

The same desugar + the embedded-stdlib wasm build power the browser playground.

## Phases + effort

| # | Phase | Effort | Notes |
|---|-------|--------|-------|
| 1 | **Opt-in `;`** — newline/boundary ends a statement (`;` still valid) | **M** (risk) | ASI-style boundary logic in `parse_block`; reuses `statement_incomplete`'s idea. **Scope lever**: universal `;`-optional is **MH** (touches all parsing, must not regress the 2100-test corpus); script-mode-only is **M** but inconsistent. |
| 2 | **Opt-in `main`** — loose top-level statements → synthesized `fn main()` | **M** | Wrap logic exists in the REPL (`starts_top_level_def` + wrap); here it's a file-level source pre-transform. Depends on phase 1. |
| 3 | **`print`/`println` of any value** | **S–M** | `"{expr}"` already renders every type; the work is letting `print` *accept* any type statically (a `Display`-like bound, or an any-value path). Today `println(42

title: Secret Benchmarking
body_excerpt:
## Request
Enigma Secret Contracts enable apps to compute over encrypted data. One simple use-case for this is “secret benchmarking”. This is a database of encrypted data that allows users to compare data they have access to with other data sets. For example, a database of 500 quotes for a service. A user could submit a quote she received, and get back which percentile her quote falls within (i.e., more expensive than 90% of other quotes). [Note: this use-case is similar to "secret Data Validation", but with additional complexity.]

## Solution Description
This solution should deploy a contract that accommodates two types of users: data providers, and data users. A data provider should be able to submit a list of values (Id, hours, rate). A data user should be able to submit a single value (Id, hour, rate). The contract should encrypt and return the percentile within which the data user’s value falls. 

This will involve:

- Writing a Secret Contract in Rust and deploying it to the Enigma Discovery network that handles the logic for the application and functions as the encrypted storage. 
- Using the  Enigma-JS client to encrypt and transmit the data provider’s dataset to the secret contract.
- Using the  Enigma-JS client to encrypt and transmit the data user’s datapoint to the secret contract, receive the correct output and successfully decrypt the result locally.
- Creating two UIs: for data providers, and data users. 


## Implementation Details and Data Flow

1. Data Provider (user A) submits a dataset with [task ID, hours, rate] via an UI. [Note: this can be filler data, but should resemble something like: 4353 (ID), 32 (total hours), 123 (hourly rate)] Data Providers should be able to enter a "task name" to title the data set.

title: fix(memory): reward-LIVE re-rank can partially undo RRF fusion order [#23][#11]
body_excerpt:
## Context
Non-blocking future-watch surfaced by S4 (#23) code review. The recall transform now does **fuse-then-rerank**: `rrfFuse`(semantic, structural) → S1 exclusion → `rerankByReward` → top-N. `rerankByReward` (sub-epic ①, #11) sorts by raw per-page `baseScore × rewardFactor`. Because RRF produces a *rank-based* consensus order (not a comparable magnitude), a subsequent sort on raw `baseScore` can partially **undo** the fused rank order.

## Why it's dormant today
`SHIPPED_REWARD_MODE='shadow'` → `rewardFactor` is forced neutral and `rerankByReward` is effectively identity, so fuse-then-rerank preserves the RRF order. **No live impact now.** This only bites when the reward mode is flipped to LIVE (the gated, deferred ① flip — needs the real-data lift gate + operator ratification).

## What to do (when reward goes LIVE)
Revisit the interaction so reward re-rank composes with RRF rather than overriding it — e.g. fold the reward factor INTO the RRF score (rank-aware), or re-rank within RRF-rank bands, rather than a raw-magnitude sort over the fused set. Add a test that a fused order is not inverted by a live reward factor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When `SHIPPED_REWARD_MODE` is LIVE, the reward re-rank composes with (does not invert) the RRF-fused order.
- [ ] A test pins fuse-then-rerank order stability under a non-neutral reward factor.

## Blocked by
- Gated on the ① reward-mode LIVE flip (`docs/eval/0001-reward-lift-gate.md`). Do NOT action until that flip is on the table.

**Goals**
- Establish a baseline benchmark suite for all platform API endpoints
- Measure latency (p50, p95, p99), throughput (req/s), and error rate under load
- Identify bottlenecks before they surface in production
- Produce a reproducible report that can be re-run on future builds for regression tracking

**Acceptance Criteria**

**Scope**
- [ ] All endpoints under `/api/` are included in the benchmark suite
- [ ] Each endpoint is tested with realistic payload sizes drawn from production schema
- [ ] Auth-protected routes are benchmarked using a dedicated benchmark test token

**Tool & Setup**
- [ ] Benchmarking tool is configured (e.g. `autocannon`, `k6`, or `wrk`) and committed to the repo under `/benchmarks`

- [ ] A `.env.benchmark` template is documented so contributors can configure the target host

**Metrics Captured Per Endpoint**
- [ ] p50, p95, p99 latency (ms)
- [ ] Requests per second (peak and sustained)

- [ ] Time to first byte (TTFB)

**Output**
- [ ] Results are written to `/benchmarks/results/` as JSON and a human-readable markdown summary
- [ ] PR includes the markdown summary in the description

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
body_excerpt:
# Star Wars: The Clone Wars

**

Average Review: 8.5/10 (1619 votes)

Yoda, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, Mace Windu and other Jedi Knights lead the Grand Army of the Republic against the droid army of the Separatists.

![backdrop](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/e1nWfnnCVqxS2LeTO3dwGyAsG2V.jpg)

Streaming On: Disney Plus

Cast: Matt Lanter, James Arnold Taylor, Ashley Eckstein, Dee Bradley Baker, Tom Kane, Matthew Wood

Keywords: space opera


<details>
<summary>Triggers</summary>

- pets die: General Grievous’ pet alien monster dies, it’s obvious that he’s distressed by this. 
- bugs: Geonosians are basically humanoid bugs and are featured throughout the series, but especially early in season 2 
- dead animals: There are several scenes where animal-like alien species are killed 
- dragons dying: There is a Godzilla-type creature called the Zillo Beast who is killed in a King Kong-esque finale 
- animals (besides dog/cat/horse) dying: In episode 10 of Season 1 General Grievous has a large pet alien creature named Gor, Gor is killed by two Jedi and Grievous is shown to be upset by this. 
- snakes: One episode has a fairly comical snake character who speaks in a silly voice but has evil motivations. He is never scary or particularly threatening. 
- spiders: One character is a sort of humanoid spider 
- child abandonment 
- gaslighting: The whole war is about gaslighting Anakin skywalker to turning to the darkside. 
- stalking 
- child abuse: There is child marriage late in S4; a villain who we are meant to find repulsive kidnaps a young girl for his bride. The girl never makes it to him, however. 
- drug use: No specific characters use drugs but there are mentions of spice and spice dealing (a fictional drug, implied to be kind of like weed, in the star wars universe) 
- alcohol abuse: Almost every episode that features pirates, bounty hunters, and the criminal underworld include drunkenness 
- restraints 
- amputation: During s5ep1 Savage Opress gets his arm cut off. It is pretty graphic during this scene (no blood still) so if this is one of your triggers I'd stay away from that episode. It happens a few more times but that is the one that sticks out the most (and is the most graphic) 
- people being burned alive: In "Landing at Point Rain" it shows clones attacking Geonosians with flamethrowers
 
- buried alive: Barriss and Ahsoka are buried alive but manage to escape 
- torture: Torture is used infrequently but strongly as a tactic by evil characte

title: [Bounty Claim] PR Review - RustChain PR #5519 (Bounty #73)
body_excerpt:
Code review bounty claim for RustChain PR #5519.

Reviewer: @kekehanshujun
RTC wallet: `RTC02811ff5e2bb4bb4b95eee44c5429cd9525496e7`

Reviewed PR:
https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain/pull/5519

Review URL:
https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain/pull/5519#pullrequestreview-4304515547

Outcome:
Requested changes.

Finding:
The PR moves Python SDK signed transfers to `/wallet/transfer/signed`, but the retained `fee` argument is silently discarded. `RustChainClient.transfer_signed()` does not send `fee_rtc`, and `RustChainWallet.sign_transfer()` signs the legacy no-fee canonical message. The node route parses `fee_rtc` and reconstructs a v2 signed message that includes `fee`, falling back to legacy only when fee is zero. As implemented, a caller passing `fee=1` believes they authorized a fee, but the SDK sends no fee and the signature does not bind it.

Direct probe on the PR branch:

- `wallet.sign_transfer(..., fee=1)` returned a payload containing `"fee": 1`
- `client.wallet_transfer_with_wallet(..., fee=1)` posted to `/wallet/transfer/signed`
- captured request payload lacked `fee_rtc`

Suggested fix:
Either send `fee_rtc` and sign the node's v2 canonical JSON shape including `fee`, or remove/deprecate `fee` from these SDK paths so nonzero fees cannot be silently ignored. Add a regression asserting `wallet_transfer_with_wallet(..., fee=1)` includes `fee_rtc` and signs that fee.

Validation performed:

- `PYTHONPATH=sdk/python python -m pytest sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\tests\test_client.py::TestRustChainClientTransfer sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\tests\test_wallet.py::TestRustChainWalletTransfer -q` -> 5 passed
- `PYTHONPATH=sdk/python python -m pytest sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\tests\test_client.py -q` -> 20 passed
- `python -m py_compile sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\client.py sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\wallet.py sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\tests\test_client.py sdk\python\rustchain_sdk\tests\test_wallet.py` -> passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD -- sdk/python/rustchain_sdk/client.py sdk/python/rustchain_sdk/wallet.py sdk/python/rustchain_sdk/tests/test_client.py sdk/python/rustchain_sdk/tests/test_wallet.py sdk/python/README.md` -> passed

title: research: add lean PDD prompt mode with token audit
body_excerpt:
Related public work: #1431, #1439, #1273, #1357, #1359

## Business value

PDD prompt structure should preserve source-truth semantics without spending tokens on repeated boilerplate that does not improve the generated change. A lean PDD prompt mode gives the public project a measurable way to reduce prompt cost while preserving bounded output, verifier, and source-truth contracts.

This matters for multi-shot and routing work because token overhead compounds with `k`: every unnecessary prompt token is paid once per candidate.

## Current public state

Public `main` has model/cost primitives and context-compression work, but no public lean PDD prompt mode:

- `pdd/data/llm_model.csv`, `pdd/llm_invoke.py`, and global CLI options expose model/cost-related controls.
- #1357/#1359 track output-inclusive token/cost estimates.
- #1439 tracks budgeted context selection and compression research.
- #1431 tracks routing across model, harness, thinking, and multi-shot count.
- The public repo does not currently have the private RQ5 harness paths referenced by the source issue, so this issue should land against public code paths or a new publishable `research/` harness.

## Requirements

- Add a selectable lean PDD prompt mode for the public generation path or a publishable research harness.
- Keep the default mode unchanged.
- Lean mode must preserve:
  - source-truth prompt/spec/contract content,
  - allowed output files,
  - verifier command and visible test contract,
  - machine-parseable output delimiters/schema,
  - safety/non-goal constraints.
- Remove or shorten only nonessential workflow framing, duplicated narrative, and boilerplate.
- Emit a `prompt_policy.json` artifact describing:
  - mode,
  - removed sections and reason,
  - preserved contract fields,
  - source inputs and hashes.
- Emit a `prompt_token_audit.json` artifact with:
  - tokenizer/model used for counting,
  - per-task current tokens,
  - per-task lean tokens,
  - ratios,
  - aggregate ratio.
- Evaluate on a publishable frozen fixture/benchmark suite; do not depend on private corpus rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- A CLI flag, config field, or harness parameter can select `current` versus `lean` mode.
- Existing behavior is unchanged when lean mode is not selected.
- Lean mode emits both policy and token-audit artifacts.
- A fixture test proves lean mode does not drop required source-truth, output, verifier, or parseability fields.

title: `claim_rewards` payout numerator may overflow u128 (theoretically possible — needs test)
body_excerpt:
## Context

`compute_reward_payout` calculates each winner's pro-rata share of `market.reward_amount`. The
platform whitelists arbitrary SPL mints; large-supply / low-decimal tokens can produce very large
`reward_amount` and per-user `score` values (score ≤ stake amount ≤ u64::MAX).

## Problem

The reward is computed multiply-before-divide in u128:

```rust
// claim_rewards.rs — compute_reward_payout
let reward = (user_score as u128)
    .checked_mul(market.reward_amount as u128)
    .ok_or(ErrorCode::Overflow)?
    .checked_mul(option.reward_bp as u128)
    .ok_or(ErrorCode::Overflow)?
    .checked_div(
        total_score.checked_mul(active_bp as u128).ok_or(ErrorCode::Overflow)?,
    )
    .ok_or(ErrorCode::Overflow)? as u64;
```

`user_score * reward_amount` alone can reach ~`u64::MAX² ≈ u128::MAX`; multiplying by
`reward_bp` (up to 10_000) can overflow u128 before the division that would have produced a
result ≤ `reward_amount`.

## Theoretical reachability

Not adversarial — configuration + token supply dependent. Example: if
`user_score * reward_amount > u128::MAX / 10_000 ≈ 3.4×10³⁴`, the second `checked_mul` returns
`Overflow` and `claim_rewards` reverts permanently for that winner.

Whether this is reachable in practice for realistic token decimals/supply is **unverified** —
needs a test.

## Impact

If reachable: winning staker's payout permanently unclaimable; `close_stake_account` also blocked
for scored winners → reward + fee refund + rent frozen.

## Suggested directions

1. **First: add a test** (in `score.rs` unit tests or `claim_rewards` tests) that either:
   - demonstrates overflow at realistic/large token parameters, or
   - proves the intermediate product stays below `u128::MAX` under documented bounds.
2. **If confirmed reachable**: reorder to divide before the final multiply:

```rust
let base = (user_score as u128)
    .checked_mul(market.reward_amount as u128).ok_or(Overflow)?
    .checked_div(total_score).ok_or(Overflow)?;  // ≤ reward_amount
let reward = base
    .checked_mul(option.reward_bp as u128).ok_or(Overflow)?
    .checked_div(active_bp as u128).ok_or(Overflow)? as u64;
```

Still floors, still ≤ pool. Requires `total_score > 0` (see zero-total-score issue).

The presence of multiple versions (`lib.rs`, `lib_original.rs`, `secure_call_interface.rs`, `secure_call_interface_old.rs`) suggests significant refactoring occurred without proper version control or documentation. A clear migration guide and upgrade history documentation is needed for developers, auditors, and downstream integrators.

Documentation gaps:
- No `MIGRATION.md` documenting the current deployment lifecycle

title: Payment currency should normalize before intent creation
body_excerpt:
Parent Algora bounty: #743

## Bug

`apps/api/src/services/paymentService.js` returns `payload.currency` exactly as submitted. Mixed-case or whitespace-padded values such as `" USD "` are returned as non-canonical payment intent currency values.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

## Steps to reproduce

Call `createPaymentIntent` with a currency value that includes leading/trailing whitespace or uppercase characters:

```js
await createPaymentIntent({
  amount: 125,
  currency: " USD "
});
```

## Expected behavior

The payment intent should return a canonical lowercase currency value:

```json
{
  "currency": "usd"
}
```

Blank currency values should continue to default to `"usd"`.

## Actual behavior

The service returns the submitted value unchanged.

## Scope

- Keep the change limited to `apps/api/src/services/paymentService.js`.
- Add focused service-level regression coverage for currency normalization.
- Preserve the existing default `"usd"` behavior.

## Validation plan

- `node --test apps/api/src/tests/paymentService.test.js`
- `npm test --workspace apps/api`
- `npm run build --workspace apps/web`
- `git diff --check`

## Safety

No payout, contact, credential, wallet, or off-platform payment details should be posted publicly.

Refs #743 and #7710.

title: Keep Full-Res Version of Edited Images
body_excerpt:
Originally reported by Adam Dingle:

At some point I think that Shotwell should keep a full-resolution version of
each image the user has edited. This would have a number of benefits. It would
allow dragging/dropping to other applications  and make it easier for
us to open photos in an external editor. It would also improve
performance when browsing through photos and quite possibly when zooming as
well.

I asked on the mailing list where Shotwell should store modified copies of
photos. People didn't want Shotwell to overwrite the originals in place. It
seemed that people leaned toward keeping the modified copies in the same
directories as the originals, though this is still up for discussion.

title: Clearer ticket statuses ("active" is confusing; no "not coming" state)
body_excerpt:
## Context
The "active" ticket status is confusing, and organizers need to mark people who told them they aren't coming **without** triggering a Stripe refund mid-event.

## Findings (code)
- Current `Ticket.TicketStatus` = `PENDING`, `ACTIVE`, `CHECKED_IN`, `CANCELLED` (`src/events/models/ticket.py:601-605`) — one axis that conflates "payment confirmed" and "ready to attend" into `ACTIVE`. Check-in is captured separately (`checked_in_at`, `checked_in_by`).
- An `EventRSVP` model already exists and may partly cover attendance intent.

## Options to discuss
1. **Relabel** `ACTIVE` → `Confirmed`/`Paid` (low effort, cosmetic).
2. **Add an orthogonal `attendance_intent` field** ("expected" / "not coming" / "sick") separate from payment + check-in state (medium effort, cleanest).
3. **Lean on the existing `EventRSVP`** records instead of new ticket state.

Let's settle 1 vs 2 vs 3 here before implementation.

cc @bechtold

> 🔗 **Coordination:** frontend status-label counterpart to follow.

---
<sub>Source: Oskar Bechtold feedback session, 2026-06-14. Filed from local triage.</sub>

title: Split the spec into functional-area documents connected by an overview
body_excerpt:
## Problem

`docs/spec.md` is a single 1269-line file covering 25 top-level sections, from the trust model through the Lua API to the build order. That makes it hard to navigate, hard to maintain (a visibility change is a diff against a 1269-line monolith), and hard to link into — issues cite line numbers that drift on every edit. It's also the one artifact every other change leans on, so the friction is paid constantly.

The proposal: split it into functional-area documents under `docs/`, with a single `overview.md` as the hub that frames the system and links out to each area. Future work and known limitations move out of the spec and into issues as part of the same pass.

## Proposed structure

A starting split for discussion — grouped by the system's functional areas, mapping the current sections:

- **`overview.md`** — Goals, Architectural principles, a high-level Trust model summary, and the TOC linking the area docs.
- **`trust-and-authority.md`** — Trust model (full detail), Clients and the server boundary.
- **`data-model.md`** — Data model, Naming conventions, Identity and participants.
- **`visibility.md`** — Visibility.
- **`conversations-and-briefs.md`** — Conversations and contexts, System prompt, Contextual briefs.
- **`events-and-storage.md`** — Event sourcing, Storage and materialization, Time.
- **`write-path.md`** — Write path and regeneration, Concurrency.
- **`agent-loop.md`** — Agent loop and tool protocol, Server API and turn lifecycle, Lua API.
- **`lifecycle.md`** — Initialization and lifecycle.
- **`observability-and-testing.md`** — Observability, Testability and abstraction boundaries, Validation and the eval harness.
- **`roadmap.md`** — Build order.

Each area doc is ~100-200 lines and self-contained enough to review in isolation.

## What leaves the spec

Two kinds of content move out of the spec as part of this split:

- **The visibility-regression appendix is removed.** Its scenarios are implemented as eval fixtures in `crates/eval/src/scenarios/` (`privacy.rs`, `compaction.rs`, `identity.rs`, and the rest), so the spec is duplicating the fixture inventory. The spec's job is to describe the architecture and *how* the system is evaluated, not enumerate the current tests. Before dropping, verify each appendix scenario has a code counterpart; any that don't get moved to code, not kept in the spec.
- **Known limitations and Future directions move to the issue tracker.** We're generally moving future work to issues so it's trackab

# Bounty: Reproducible Wallet Performance Test Harness

**Tier:** L — 150,000 XTM

## Description

Build a reproducible test harness that measures `minotari-cli` wallet performance across three modes: old wallet (`minotari_console_wallet` via gRPC), new wallet (`minotari-cli` library with offline signing), and payment processor (batch 1-to-many transactions via `minotari-cli`).

Implementation approach is up to you — Rust, Python, shell scripts, or any combination — as long as the results are reproducible and verifiable by a third party running the same harness against the same network.

## Deliverables

1. **Harness source code** in a new repo, buildable and runnable by anyone with access to a funded wallet on Esmeralda testnet.
2. **Run instructions** — complete, step-by-step, no implicit knowledge.
3. **Baseline result profile** — a structured report generated by running the harness, committed alongside the code, serving as proof the harness works and as a reference point for future comparisons.

## Wallet Modes

1. **Old Wallet (`minotari_console_wallet`)** — harness manages the wallet process lifecycle (spawn, wait for ready, run tests, tear down) and interacts via gRPC.
2. **New Wallet (`minotari-cli` library)** — uses the `minotari` crate directly: local UTXO selection, `sign_locked_transaction`, broadcast via HTTP RPC to a base node. No external wallet process.
3. **Payment Processor** — uses the new wallet's batch transaction capability to send 1-to-many transactions.

# cs.SE updates on arXiv.org, Tue, 07 May 2024 04:00:15 +0000

## [CodeGRAG: Extracting Composed Syntax Graphs for Retrieval Augmented Cross-Lingual Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02355) [[pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.02355.pdf)]

Authors: Kounianhua Du, Renting Rui, Huacan Chai, Lingyue Fu, Wei Xia, Yasheng Wang, Ruiming Tang, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

Tags: `LLM`

 Utilizing large language models to generate codes has shown promising meaning in software development revolution. Despite the intelligence shown by the general large language models, their specificity in code generation can still be improved due to the syntactic gap and mismatched vocabulary existing among natural language and different programming languages. In addition, programming languages are inherently logical and complex, making them hard to be correctly generated. Existing methods rely on multiple prompts to the large language model to explore better solutions, which is expensive. In this paper, we propose Syntax Graph Retrieval Augmented Code Generation (CodeGRAG) to enhance the performance of **LLM**s in single-round code generation tasks. CodeGRAG extracts and summarizes the control flow and data flow of code blocks to fill the gap between programming languages and natural language. The extracted external structural knowledge models the inherent flows of code blocks, which can facilitate **LLM**s for better understanding of code syntax and serve as a bridge among different programming languages. CodeGRAG significantly improves the code generation ability of **LLM**s and can even offer performance gain for cross-lingual code generation, e.g., C++ for Python.

## Thread

https://www.reddit.com/r/ecommerce/comments/1stush7/solo_founder_with_0_followers_i_know_my_audience/

## What `tider` generated

```text
I agree with the “you don’t need organic to run FB ads” takes, but I wouldn’t wait on content either—start ads now using simple trust-first creatives you can make without being on camera, and give your Page a minimal “trust hub” so clicks don’t bounce.

What to make first (no face needed):
- 6–15s hands-only demo: show scale in your hand, a quick use, a close-up of texture/color. Big captions, clear benefit, one CTA.
- Photo carousel: 3–5 strong images with short overlay text (problem → outcome), final card with offer/FAQ.
- Social proof: screenshot a real review, add product photo, and a clear “Shop now” line.

Run paid now: Sales objective, broad 35+ on Facebook placements, 2–3 creatives in one ad set, small daily budget. Let the first week tell you which angle (demo vs proof vs benefit) pulls. Once you have traffic, add a simple retargeting ad that leans hard on reviews/returns/shipping clarity.

Hiring: hold the social media manager. If you spend, spend on assets—either a UGC creator to shoot 3–5 clips or a lightweight editor to turn your raw phone shots into usable posts/ads. That’s the highest ROI early.
```

## What I posted / wanted instead

The reply should have more clearly surfaced the Kova lens:

- real product visuals should not just be ad creatives
- they can be reused across ads, the Page, PDPs, and follow-up
- the same capture solves trust and content reuse

The current output is solid general FB-advice, but the Kova angle is barely visible.

## Gap

The prompt is allowing `--context=kova` to behave like a soft supporting lens instead of a strong framing constraint on threads about content creation / ads / social strategy.

This thread is a good Kova fit because it is specifically about:

- creating trust-first creatives without being on camera
- deciding what to produce first
- whether to skip ahead with ads
- whether hiring early makes sense

That should have triggered a stronger “same visual proof can be reused across channels” frame.

## Desired behavior

When `--context=kova` is present and the thread is about content creation, ads, social strategy, or trust assets, `Best Pick` should explicitly mention that the same real product visuals can be reused across ads, the Page, PDPs, and follow-up.
